# Jim Crow Museum

> > The Jim Crow Museum at Ferris State University uses objects of intolerance to teach tolerance and promote social justice through the examination of racist artifacts and anti-Black imagery.

Located at Ferris State University in Michigan, the museum houses thousands of racist artifacts, memorabilia, and caricatures spanning from the Jim Crow era to contemporary times. Founded by Dr. David Pilgrim, the museum serves as an educational resource for understanding the history of racial stereotypes, segregation, and ongoing racism in America.

## Key Topics

- Jim Crow era
- Racist imagery and caricatures
- Racial stereotypes
- Civil rights history
- Anti-Black imagery
- Ferris State University
- Educational anti-racism programming
- Mammy caricature
- Minstrel shows and coon songs
- Segregation artifacts
- Cultural appropriation
- Contemporary racist merchandise
- African American pioneers
- Social justice education
- Race relations

## Core Educational Resources

- [The Mammy Caricature - Anti-black Imagery](https://jimcrowmuseum.ferris.edu/mammies/homepage.htm): Mammy caricature analysis: Anti-black imagery and slavery stereotypes
- [Educational Programming](https://jimcrowmuseum.ferris.edu/education/index.htm): Anti-racism education programs, tours, and curriculum resources at FSU
- [Deconstructing Racist Images](https://jimcrowmuseum.ferris.edu/links/deconstructing.htm): Educational resources analyzing racist imagery with Kara Walker & others
- [Time of Change Exhibit](https://jimcrowmuseum.ferris.edu/davidsonexhibit/index.htm): Bruce Davidson civil rights photography traveling exhibit at FSU

## Historical Racist Imagery and Artifacts

- [What Were Coon Songs? - 2005](https://jimcrowmuseum.ferris.edu/question/2005/may.htm): Coon songs history: Minstrel shows and 19th century racist music
- [Nigger Head Oysters - 2017](https://jimcrowmuseum.ferris.edu/question/2017/august.htm): Racist product branding history: Niggerhead Oysters and NAACP activism
- ['Favorite' Object? - 2012](https://jimcrowmuseum.ferris.edu/question/2012/november.htm): Curator Q&A on museum segregation artifacts and teaching tools
- [A Collector's Musings - 2005](https://jimcrowmuseum.ferris.edu/letters/2005/musings.htm): Collector's perspective on racist artifacts and folk art memorabilia
- [Uncle Remus - 2007](https://jimcrowmuseum.ferris.edu/letters/2007/remus.htm): Visitor letter examining Uncle Remus folklore and cultural appropriation

## Contemporary Racism and Ongoing Manifestations

- [Instant Rapper - …and it doesn't stop](https://jimcrowmuseum.ferris.edu/dontstop/rapper.htm): Instant Rapper Kit: Contemporary racist merchandise and stereotypes
- ["I'd Rather Celebrate James Earl Ray Day" bumper sticker](https://jimcrowmuseum.ferris.edu/dontstop/jamesearlray.htm): James Earl Ray bumper sticker: Modern hate merchandise targeting MLK
- [Italian Version of "Mammy" - 2010](https://jimcrowmuseum.ferris.edu/letters/2010/italy.htm): Correspondence about Mammy stereotypes in Italian commercial imagery
- [Ties That Bind - Jim Crow Museum in the News](https://jimcrowmuseum.ferris.edu/links/newslist/gambit2.htm): Jefferson Parish noose necktie controversy and prosecutorial misconduct

## Civil Rights History and Resistance

- [The Southern Manifesto - 2006](https://jimcrowmuseum.ferris.edu/question/2006/july.htm): Southern Manifesto opposition to Brown v. Board school integration
- [Reverend Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. - 2015](https://jimcrowmuseum.ferris.edu/question/2015/January.htm): MLK's religious identity, faith-based activism, and misattributed quotes
- [Banning "To Kill a Mockingbird"? - 2007](https://jimcrowmuseum.ferris.edu/question/2007/may.htm): Museum response to censorship debates around To Kill a Mockingbird

## African American Pioneers and Achievements

- [Fred B. Pelham - 2018](https://jimcrowmuseum.ferris.edu/question/2018/july.htm): Fred B. Pelham: First Black U of Michigan engineering graduate pioneer
- [Russell A. Dixon - 2017](https://jimcrowmuseum.ferris.edu/question/2017/January.htm): Russell Dixon: Early African American student at Ferris Institute

## Optional

- [Subverting "Civilized" Values - 2005](https://jimcrowmuseum.ferris.edu/letters/2005/civilized.htm): London art student letter on colonial imagery and racial caricatures
